about: The diagnostic codes production code of the solve crates constructs, read from those sources by tools/validation/diagnostic_codes.py, with a hand-made classification of each. What a code is, what is read and what is not, and what the test establishes are in scope. The scanner writes code, crates, severity, first_site, sites and messages; classification, reason, unsure, candidates, named_by, named_by_coverage and named_by_statement are hand-made and kept by --write, as is pinned_sites. The test cannot check that a text covers a refusal, only that it mentions a code: each naming carries a hand-made coverage, whole or partial, and only a whole naming counts as naming the refusal.
first_site: the first raising site resolved by type (and, where a mapping is involved, by the arm its argument selects); a site resolved only by a method's name carries by_name, one that may raise any arm of a mapping carries any_arm, and neither is chosen as first while another exists; sites_by_name_only says that every site was resolved by name
named_by_coverage: for a code named by a LIM entry: {"coverage": "whole" or "partial", "reason"}; a partial naming counts as unnamed

classes.absent_capability: the product refuses or withholds because it does not do something a user could reasonably ask of it (a family, an analysis, a combination or an option not built, or not built on this route)
classes.input_error: the document is incomplete, inconsistent or invalid and a user can correct it to obtain the result
classes.numerical_standing: the solve ran and the code states how far the result can be relied on, or that it did not converge or is ill-conditioned
classes.disclosure: a non-blocking statement of what was done or not applied, which refuses nothing
classes.internal: an invariant, a wire or version mismatch, something no document a user authors should reach

named_by: for an absent_capability code, the LIM-nnn entry of docs/RELEASE_LIMITATIONS_v1.0.md that names the code, or "unnamed"; null for the other classes
named_by_statement: the product texts that name the code, as a list, or null when none does: {"status": "in_product", "text", "where", "coverage", "coverage_reason"} for text the product publishes today (a formulation_basis limitation), whole or partial as for named_by_coverage; {"status": "planned", "statement", "subject", "lands_with"} for a per-document limitation statement not yet in the product, which names nothing today. Planned statements may name codes of any class.
pinned_site: an entry of pinned_sites: a code position whose value the scanner cannot resolve but the source settles, pinned by hand: {"file", "at", "why", "site_text", "values", "reason", "anchors": [{"file", "text"}]}. A pin holds only while the scan leaves a site unresolved with that file, at and why on the line where site_text stands (once in the file), and each anchor text stands exactly once in its file; a holding pin turns the site into sites of its values. Any other unresolved site fails the test.

scope.unit: The unit of this table is the code: the value of the code field of a diagnostic, finding, refusal or reason record that production code of the scanned crates constructs. There is one record per distinct value, whatever its spelling.
scope.what_in_the_table_means: The table is therefore a superset of the codes a solve publishes. That a code is in the table does not mean that a person can meet the refusal it names. A limitation is declared for a refusal a person can meet, and that needs its own trace, from the trigger through the route taken to the output consumed, when the limitation is drafted.
